LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should a text be well punctuated? 2. How does wrong punctuation affect writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy as learners gains the confidence to use punctuation marks correctly in speech and in writing.

● Critical thinking as learners figures out when to use the comma, apostrophe and capital letter in a text.

Values:
Respect: A learner enhances this as they value each other’s’ contributions during group work to

punctuate a given text using commas, apostrophes, and capital letters.

Link to other subjects:

Using commas, apostrophes, and capital letters is linked to using commas, apostrophes, and capital

letters in Kiswahili, German, French

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Audio-visual recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology
